draft.title: Octavian after Caesar's death
card: Julius Caesar was assassinated in March 44 BC. His will named his great-nephew Octavian, then aged 18, as his adopted son and main heir.
Octavian took the name Gaius Julius Caesar. The name mattered because many Romans, especially Caesar's veterans and soldiers, were loyal to Caesar's memory.
Octavian paid the bequests Caesar left to the people of Rome and won over Caesar's veterans. He raised a private army from them, though he held no office at the time.
Octavian then used this support and military force to challenge Mark Antony, who had been Caesar's close ally, and to win a place among Rome's leaders.
draft.remember: Octavian turned an inheritance of name and loyalty into political and military power.

a.q: Why was the name Caesar so useful to Octavian in 44 BC?
opts: It won him the loyalty of Caesar's veterans and soldiers
It made him consul as soon as Caesar died
It gave him control of the Senate's votes
It made Mark Antony hand over his own army
a.why: Many soldiers and veterans were loyal to Caesar, so his adopted son could draw on that loyalty and raise an army. The name did not give him an office or the Senate's votes, and it did not hand him Antony's forces.
a.clue: Think about who was still loyal to Caesar after his death.

b.q: Which action best shows Octavian using Caesar's legacy to gain power after 44 BC?
opts: Raising a private army from Caesar's veterans
Winning the Battle of Actium against Cleopatra
Taking the name Augustus from the Senate
Sharing power with Antony and Lepidus by law
b.why: Octavian had no office in 44 BC, so he built an army from Caesar's veterans, who followed him because of Caesar's name. The other options are later events or are taught as separate points.
b.clue: Which action happened soon after the will was read, when Octavian held no office?

a.best: It won him the loyalty of Caesar's veterans and soldiers

b.best: Raising a private army from Caesar's veterans

a.why: Many soldiers and veterans were loyal to Caesar, so his adopted son could draw on that loyalty and raise an army. The name did not give him an office or the Senate's votes, and Antony was a rival he had to challenge, not an ally who gave up his forces.
a.clue: Octavian held no office in 44 BC. What could a name give him instead?

b.q: Which action best shows Octavian using Caesar's legacy to gain power in 44 BC?
opts: Raising a private army from Caesar's veterans
Being elected consul by the people in 44 BC
Taking over Antony's army by a friendly deal
Holding back Caesar's gifts to pay his own troops
b.why: Octavian held no office in 44 BC, so he built an army from veterans who followed him because of Caesar's name. He was not consul then, he challenged Antony rather than making a deal with him, and he paid Caesar's bequests to the people instead of keeping them.
b.clue: Which option fits a young man with no office but many followers?
